label: 0060 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 53 windows): 0059 with five more volcanic sources (Hakone, Izu-Oshima, Kirishima, Aso, deep Unzen), uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0059 with five more volcanic pressure (Mogi) sources: Hakone (4 km), Izu-Oshima (7 km), Kirishima (8.2 km), Aso (4.1 km) and deep Unzen (15 km); the Kyushu positions and depths are those of Munekane and Ichimura (2026, Earth Planets Space 78:251). Each source, like the existing Aira, Izu (Miyake-jima) and Usu sources, has an independent volume rate in every window, with the same prior sd (about 8 × 10⁶ m³/yr). They were chosen by a screen of 0059's residuals that found Mogi-shaped, multi-site signals at these five volcanoes, matching their known unrest. Residuals within 15 km fall from 14.2 to 8.4 mm/yr at Izu-Oshima, 6.4 to 3.8 at Kirishima, 5.9 to 4.1 at Aso, 11.0 to 9.1 at Hakone and 3.8 to 3.4 at Unzen (medians over the windows); the network fit improves by 1%. Kirishima reinflates after its January 2011 eruption and again in 2017–18 and 2024–25; Aso deflates slowly before 2016 and inflates in 2019, 2021 and early 2024; Unzen's deep source inflates in 1997–99 and then stops. Coupling, the BEL, Hyuga-nada afterslip and the slow slip episodes are unchanged (within 0.08 in coupling and 0.01 in Mw), except on the 2016 Kumamoto fault, whose slip near Aso changes by about half in the months after the earthquake: the Aso source and the fault's end trade off there. Held-out windows are predicted better than by 0059 (window cross-validation +520, better in 42 of 53 windows), and each source adds to that: deep Unzen +181, Izu-Oshima +128, Hakone +101, Aso +64 and Kirishima +48.
